newsitem.title: GHANA: Several hurt in pre-poll violence in north Ghana.
newsitem.headline: Several hurt in pre-poll violence in north Ghana.

text.p: Several people have been wounded in northern Ghana, some seriously, in the first politicial violence of the run-up to the West African country's national elections in December, residents say.

The violence in the volatile northern town of Tamale broke out on Friday and Saturday. Witnesses said young supporters of the ruling National Democratic Congress and the main opposition parties fought with home-made rifles, cutlasses and stones.
President Jerry Rawlings, who staged two coups and then won election as president, stands for a final four-year term on December 7. Legislative elections will be held on the same date.
Tamale, which has a reputation for violent communal conflict, had been calm since Sunday, residents told Reuters by telephone.
Tamale hospital was not immediately available for comment on the nature of the injuries. Witnesses and newspapers said shots were heard as hundreds of youths clashed on Saturday night.

The trouble began late Friday when windows were smashed on a truck broadcasting ruling party songs as it tried to go through a rally of the opposition Great Alliance. Ruling party activists smashed the windows of a bus hired by the opposition alliance.
The Great Alliance is a coalition of Ghana's main opposition New Patriotic Party and People's Convention Party.

Monday's Daily Graphic newspaper said the Northern Regional Police Commander, Patrick Agboba, had told all political parties to submit campaign programmes to enable police to contain political unrest in Tamale.
